topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Cancer Progression Framework
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's learning objectives, contextualises cancer progression within a genetic framework, and outlines the hallmarks of cancer model.

topics.label: Growth Signal Autonomy and Intracellular Cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream cascades drive autonomous proliferation and override growth-inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how blocks in terminal differentiation prevent cells from exiting the cell cycle across both hematopoietic and epithelial cancers.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cancer cells resist programmed cell death by altering the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins regulated by p53.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells achieve replicative immortality by maintaining telomere length and overcoming p53-mediated senescence.

topics.label: Deregulating Cellular Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the transition to complex cancer hallmarks by analyzing how tumor cells rewire cellular metabolism toward aerobic glycolysis and altered Krebs cycle function.

topics.label: Inducing Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how developing tumors stimulate new blood vessel growth to overcome hypoxia and nutrient limitations.

topics.label: Metastatic Cascade and Dissemination
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the biological mechanisms, circulatory pathways, and diagnostic detection of cancer metastasis.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reflecting on the convergence of cancer hallmarks, referencing recent literature, and opening for questions.
